pr_title: [WIP] feat(tsdb): Add support for deleting OOO data
pr_body:
### Description
This PR introduces the ability to delete out-of-order (OOO) data within a specified time range. The feature extends the existing Delete function in the Head struct, allowing users to remove both in-order and OOO samples from memory and optionally from the Write-Ahead Log (WAL).

### Related Issue
Closes #11790 

### Proposed Changes
1. Added `DeleteRange` method to `OOOChunk` to remove samples in a specified time range.
2. Extended the Delete method in the Head struct to also remove OOO data, if present.
3. Added WAL support for OOO data deletion (Optional).

### Proof Manifests
#### How to Test
1. Execute `curl -X POST -g 'http://localhost:9090/api/v1/admin/tsdb/delete_series?match[]=<MERTIC>'`, replace MERTIC with the metric you want to delete

pr_comments:
I'm a bit wary about how the tombstone doesn't get removed from the OOO head until after compaction - this would mean we wouldn't be able to insert OOO data for the deleted timerange for a while after the deletion request. I think it might be easy to think you're adding more samples but for it to be silently deleted.

If we wanted the deletion to work "perfectly", we'd keep track of the last OOO sample added before the deletion request in the tombstone and only remove that sample or samples that were inserted earlier. But this would be inefficient and complicated to keep track of. 

A possibly simpler approach could be to only delete samples from chunks that were mmapped before the deletion request. I'm not sure how easy it is to keep track of the last mmapped chunk and handle that in a tombstone, but the [WBL does some mmap ref tracking](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/9825a80498de18183cdded8074c2a7c908182428/tsdb/head_append.go#L942) that we might be able to take inspiration from. I'll do a bit more digging on this, but won't have time until next week.

This isn't perfect - the OOO samples that haven't been mmapped yet can't be deleted until a new ooo head chunk is cut. But imo it's better to hold on to more data than necessary than to drop more data than necessary - happy to hear thoughts about this suggestion.

Looked a bit more into how we could only delete data from mmapped chunks.

In the [`Delete()` method in head.go](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/9825a80498de18183cdded8074c2a7c908182428/tsdb/head.go#L1488) we could look up the last mmap ref in `series.ooo.oooMmappedChunks` and add that info to a tombstone. One thing to keep in mind is how the new field might affect the tombstone encoding when doing the WAL replay.

The querying bit is harder. We want to filter out samples from chunks with a ref < tombstone.lastMmapRef. The problem is that the [ooo chunk reader merges several chunks together](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/6b8e9453881bffe5fe3aec99a6f3462676a95489/tsdb/ooo_head_read.go#L265) before [returning an iterable to the series iterator](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/6b8e9453881bffe5fe3aec99a6f3462676a95489/tsdb/querier.go#L701) and the tombstones are applied after the chunks are merged and at that point you don't have the proper chunk refs anymore. It's possible to add the logic but you'd have to make a bunch of changes.

If we want to go down this route, we could mmap the current head chunk if it's within the deletion range and use that as the last mmapped ref in the tombstone. But if a lot of series are being deleted, this could be slow.

issue_context.title: Deleting data points older than TSDB min date with 'delete_series' API endpoint fails
issue_context.body:
### What did you do?

1. Set `out_of_order_time_window` in storage configuration to allow the storage of data points that are older than the TSDB's minimum timestamp by a certain amount of time.
2. Generate and store some data points with timestamps older than the TSDB's minimum timestamp.
3. Use the` /api/v1/admin/tsdb/delete_series` API endpoint to delete the data points, specifying a match parameter that matches the data points you created.
4. Observe that the data points are not deleted.

### What did you expect to see?

When I use the `/api/v1/admin/tsdb/delete_series` API endpoint to delete the data points I created, I expect Prometheus to delete all data points matching the specified match parameters, regardless of their timestamps.

### What did you see instead? Under which circumstances?

The `delete_series` API does not delete data points with timestamps older than the TSDB's minimum timestamp.

### System information

Linux 6.0.11-300.fc37.x86_64 x86_64

Hi @codesome @jesusvazquez, I would like to work on this.

I tried to reproduce the issue and was able to successfully do reproduce it. I was going through the design document - [Support for out-of-order samples in the TSDB ](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Kppm7qL9C-BJB1j6yb6-9ObG3AbdZnFUBYPNNWwDBYM/edit#heading=h.unv3m5m27vuc), I read under "**Non goals for the initial version**" that deletion is not supported for OOO data. Also, while going through the code and one of your blog which quoted "_any deletions to the data are stored as tombstones in a separate file while the data still stays on disk. So when the tombstones are touching more than some % of the series, we need to remove that data from the disk_" and Prometheus doesn't support **Tombstones for out of order metrics**. 

Could you provide some insight into why the support for tombstones for out-of-order metrics has not been implemented, particularly if there are any logical complications that have made this challenging? Also, can you please clarify whether if there are any plans to implement it in the future?

:wave: @nidhey27 

> Could you provide some insight into why the support for tombstones for out-of-order metrics has not been implemented

In all honestly it was left out at the time. The remaining parts of the out-of-order feature had already quite enough complexity and we needed to decide what to do. So we chased read, write and compaction support and then production experience with those.

> Also, can you please clarify whether if there are any plans to implement it in the future?

We definitely want deletion for out-of-order samples. But we do not have any plans for doing so in the sort term so your contribution would be really appreciated.

I know some bits of the TSDB better than others and tombstones and the deletion features is not one of my strengths. Maybe @codesome can help us here. In the meantime I'll try to investigate this whenever I get some spare time so I can also provide guidance.

Hello from the bug scrub.

The PR has some review comments that need to be addressed. Keeping this open for now.

review_comments:
This is adding 8 bytes per ooo chunk which will increase total memory usage of prometheus instances.

What could be done is having a global ooo tombstones object so we dont need to have one per chunk but then we have an issue when:

```
insertOOO(t0,t1,t2,t3,t4,t5)
delete(t1,t2) // added to global ooo tombstones list
insertOOO(t1,t2)
query(t0,t5) // returns t0,t3,t4,t5 omitting t1,t2 because the global list doesnt know that the last write was after the delete call
```

So I think for now we should add a comment here saying this adds 8 bytes per chunk and a post-optimization can be to have a global list that also tracks ooo chunk references and that will save memory usage.
These are in-order samples rather than out of order samples - we need to add a sample with a newer timestamp before adding these samples.

This will only query for in-order samples - when a new BlockQuerier is created for `head`, only the in-order chunks/tombstones etc. are set in the block querier. You can see the issue if you only delete a subset of out of order samples - none of the OOO samples will appear when reading the query results. 

To read the ooo samples as well (if any exist), you could do something similar to TestOOOInsertDeleteCompactQuery where a db is created and then `db.Querier(math.MinInt64, math.MaxInt64)` is called.

Also note that `head.MinTime()` refers to the in-order min time. So there could be OOO samples in the head that have older timestamps than `head.MinTime()`. There's a `head.OOOMinTime()` function that could be used for OOO samples instead.

`head.tombstones` will only span the range of the in-order samples, as when doing a delete request, the time range is clamped to the min/max times for in-order samples (`head.MinTime()`/`head.MaxTime()` only keeps track of in-order samples):

https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/9825a80498de18183cdded8074c2a7c908182428/tsdb/head.go#L1465-L1466

We'd need to update the logic to take into account of the OOO time range too.
